# Warrant syntax v1

57 authored syntax cases for [VER04 P006a](../../VER04-warrant-language.md#11-grammar-artifacts-and-syntax-corpus-staging-p006).
Each has a source program, a syntax verdict and exact matched-subtree witnesses.
No expected answer is generated by invoking the subject parser. Feature groups
organize reviewed examples; they do not certify exhaustive language coverage.

The Python gate strictly validates field/kind/budget/duplicate/baseline rules
and emits TFV. It is a transport validator, not an independent Warrant parser.
The native consumer runs the existing shared lexer/parser against both loaded
and compiled grammars, checks authored verdicts/witnesses and compares ASTs.
An intentionally wrong-precedence grammar still parses but fails the authored
grouping witness. Whole-entry membership, not substring search, is required.

From the repository root:

```sh
python code/scripts/warrant_syntax_corpus.py --write
python code/scripts/warrant_syntax_corpus.py
python -m unittest discover -s code/scripts/tests -p test_warrant_syntax_corpus.py
```

`cases.json` is the authoring source; edit it directly and regenerate. TFV is
the runtime transport and is compared as bytes, so a CRLF file fails drift
checks. Corpus sources are limited to 4 KiB and the document to 128 cases/2 MiB;
these bounds protect this corpus workflow, not the future public source API.

The suite includes syntax-positive duplicate declarations, Bool/Int comparison
and an unreachable refinement. Later phases must reject those where specified.
No typed/checked-spec status, original-byte-span guarantee, complete source
budget enforcement, solver evidence or release approval follows from a pass.
The design inventory in `../warrant-v0` continues to describe future phases.
